data.title: Searching without borders? A Czech-Slovak dialogue between archaeologists and metal detectorists
data.excerpt: Representatives of professional institutions and of volunteer associations from Czechia and Slovakia met for an open discussion about working together in archaeology. Our Hradiská civic association took part in the project alongside the Institute of Archaeology in Brno, the Monuments Board of the Slovak Republic and the Archeo Moravia association.
data.metaTitle: Archaeologists and metal detectorists in dialogue
data.metaDescription: A Czech-Slovak discussion between archaeologists and metal detectorists about working together, with the Institute of Archaeology in Brno as partner.

children.text: The Hradiská civic association took part, together with the Institute of Archaeology in Brno, the Monuments Board of the Slovak Republic and the Archeo Moravia association, in a very interesting project whose first outcome is this discussion between archaeologists and non-specialists on the subject of cooperation between them. We shall be curious to hear your reactions. We thank Balázs Komoróczy, Peter Bisták, Jiří Ráčil and Tomáš Merta for their obliging approach.

Archaeology, metal detectors and the protection of archaeological finds are among the topics that arouse strong emotions across Europe. Approaches to metal detecting differ markedly from one country to another – as do the views of the specialist and of the general public.

Since 2018 the Institute of Archaeology of the Czech Academy of Sciences in Brno and the South Moravian Region have been developing the programme “Společnými silami za poznáním společného archeologického dědictví Jihomoravského kraje” (Joining forces to understand the shared archaeological heritage of the South Moravian Region), which creates the conditions for legal, professionally led and responsible cooperation with the public in the search for metal objects. An important partner of theirs is also the Archeo Moravia association, which brings together volunteers actively involved in rescuing archaeological finds.

The discussion meeting of representatives of professional institutions and of cooperating associations from the Czech Republic and Slovakia offered an open exchange of experience, named both the benefits and the limits of the various approaches, and gave a broader view of the possibilities of civic cooperation in archaeology. The discussion took place as part of the project “Integrovaný model občanské vědy v archeologii: odborná spolupráce, aplikace a transfer poznatků v Jihomoravském kraji” (An integrated model of citizen science in archaeology: professional cooperation, application and transfer of insights in the South Moravian Region), supported by the Regional Cooperation programme of the Czech Academy of Sciences in 2025.
